title: The treatment-side panel section, its properties and action vocabulary, the treatment-type document set row and the one-hop set read are not specified
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 017 Contract CA and mortgage document generation screens v1, sections 4, 7, 11, 12, 13 and 15; TSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v2 T3.1, T3.2, T6.1 and T-A.1; FSD S2 TDR, settlement and deed in lieu v3 A2.18; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 8, 13 and 41; context pack S2 (ownership rows of S2, naming rules); Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1, sections R5.5 and R7.2
section: Story sections 3 Preconditions, 4 Flow, 7 Acceptance criteria, 11 Data, 12.1, 12.2, 12.5 and 13 Solution plan
description: One combined row for the values the sources do not give. (1) No source gives the treatment read a panel section: TSD S2 T3.1 lists DF-TRT-001 to DF-TRT-033 and none of them is a document-set state, an action availability, a blocker message or a template version, and T-A.1 lists four treatment operations only, so the section, its property names and the action vocabulary have to be published by this story on the declared read. (2) No source says who answers the action availability: the legacy story composes the panel and the gate in one process and one recovery schema, while the target gives the documents to rwb-document and the treatment to rwb-treatment with no grant either way. (3) No source states the treatment-type set row: the legacy points at the template and merge-field catalogue by template code and at reference data for the set per treatment type, and no source names the list code, the row or the mapping of DEED_IN_LIEU and RESTRUCTURE to their template codes and legal types. (4) No source gives the shape of the set read as this service consumes it beyond the legacy in-process calls and the endpoint POST /cases/{caseId}/generated-documents of the generation engine; the set read of a case filtered by treatment is a working read of the document contract. (5) No source gives the paragraph-level behaviour of an unavailable owner inside a read that must still answer, so the partial answer of MSG-GEN-006 is this story's reading.
evidence: TSD S2 v2 T3.1 (no set, action, blocker or template-version field) and T-A.1 (four treatment operations, no panel or set sub-resource); legacy RWB-E2-017 section 11 (document and decision_log_entry fields only, treatment fields read only) and section 12 (DocumentGenerator.generate and SignatureRequests.start as in-process interfaces, no REST set read); Architecture v5 slide 13 (row S2 Treatment: T and E to P7, T to P5, no R to P5) and slide 41 (documents with P5, templates with P6); context pack S2 (S2 owns one table, four REST operations and one event, none of which is the panel or the set); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-07, DP-11 and DP-13.
proposed: Publish the panel as an optional additive property of the declared treatment read, take the set read from RWB-P5-E2017-CON with a 2 s budget and a fake, take the document types and the set row from the reference-data contract at their version, and keep every name provisional until the contract is frozen.

title: The legacy files the whole generation capability under the document module, while the target gives the treatment screen leg to rwb-treatment and the set to rwb-document
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epic 2 Story Files v5, RWB E2 017 Contract CA and mortgage document generation screens v1, sections 1, 12, 13 and 15; Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 Text Extract v1, slides 4, 8, 13 and 41; work package B2-S2-019 story line for RWB-S2-E2017-APP; sibling story RWB-P5-E2017-APP, sections 1, 3 and 12
description: Two sources place the same screen in two services. The legacy key is a P5 Document hub story: its module is P5, its package is recovery/dochub/generation, its controller adds the regenerate and send endpoints, its React components live in the document hub, and its decision records are written by the document module's DecisionLogWriter. Architecture v5 keeps the documents, the document types and the stores with P5 rwb-document, and keeps SCR-14 Treatment record and the treatment row with S2 rwb-treatment; the work package then splits the key across P5, S2, P6, P7, P4 and the integration harness and gives S2 the treatment leg of the screen with an empty acceptance-criteria list. The consequence is that one screen is answered by two services through the composite route, and that the pattern list of the S2 slice carries DP-03 while every actionable record of the key (the correction and the send) is the document service's. This story resolves it by serving the panel from the treatment read, reading the set on one hop from the document contract, and writing no record of its own.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E2-017 section 12 (POST /documents/{documentId}/regenerate and POST /treatments/{treatmentId}/signature-requests are document-module endpoints) and section 13 (package recovery/dochub/generation, GeneratedDocumentController, GenerateDocumentsPanel and GeneratedDocumentReview on SCR-14 and SCR-30, DecisionLogWriter only); Architecture v5 slide 41 (P5 documents, P6 templates) and slide 8 (screens behind gateway-bff); work package B2-S2-019 (C RWB-P5-E2017-CON, acs empty, secondary true); RWB-P5-E2017-APP sections 1, 3 and 12 (it reads the treatment through the S2 contract and owns the actions and their records).
proposed: Keep the legacy placement as the loser for the actions and their records (P5), keep the treatment gate and the screen's treatment leg with S2, serve one screen through the gateway-bff composite route with each service answering its own fact, and record that the S2 slice writes no decision record of this key.
